<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XVII.|ACCORDING TO S. LVKE.|189}}</noinclude>God commeth not vvith obseruation: {{verse|chapter=17|verse=21}}† neither shal they say, Loe here, or loe there. for loe {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ While they aske and looke for a temporal kingdom in pompe and glorie, loe their king & Messias was now among them. whose spiritual kingdom is within al the faithful that haue dominion ouer sinne.}}∷ the kingdom of God is vvithin you.

{{verse|chapter=17|verse=22}}† And he said to his Disciples, The daies vvil come vvhen you shal desire to see one day of the Sonne of man: and you shal not see. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=23}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 24, 23. Mar. 13, 21.''}}* And they vvil say to you, Loe here and loe there. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ No man must runne out of the Church after Schismatikes to heare them preach Christ in corners, Christs doctrine being open in al the world. See annot. ''Mt. 24, 23''.}}∷ Goe not, neither doe ye folovv after. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=24}}† For euen as the lightening that lighteneth from vnder heauen, vnto those partes that are vnder heauen, shineth: so shal the Sonne of man be in his day. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=25}}† But first he must suffer many things and be reiected of this generation. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=26}}† And as it came to passe in the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 7, 5.''}}* daies of Noé, so shal it be also in the daies of the Sonne of man. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=27}}† They did eate and drinke, they did marie vviues and vvere giuen to mariage euen vntil the day that Noé entred into the arke: and the floud came, and destroyed them al. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=28}}† Likevvise as it came to passe in the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 19, 24.''}}* daies of Lot: They did eate and drinke, bought and sould, planted, and builded: {{verse|chapter=17|verse=29}}† and in the day that Lot vvent out from Sodome, it rained fire and brimstone from heauen, and destroyed them all: {{verse|chapter=17|verse=30}}† according to these things it shal be in the day that the Sonne of man shal be reuealed. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=31}}† In that houre he that shal be in the house-toppe, and his vessel in the house, let him not goe dovvne to take them vp: and he that is in the field, in like maner let him not returne backe. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=32}}† Be mindeful of {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 19, 26.''}}* Lots vvife. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=33}}† VVhosoeuer seeketh to saue his life, shal lose it: and vvhosoeuer doth lose the same, shal quicken it. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=34}}† I say to you, in that night there shal be tvvo in one bed: the one shal be taken, and the other shal be left: {{verse|chapter=17|verse=35}}† tvvo vvomen shal be grinding together: the one shal be taken, and the other shal be left: tvvo in the field: the one shal be taken, and the other shal be left. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=36}}† They ansvvering say to him, VVhere Lord? {{verse|chapter=17|verse=37}}† VVho said to them, VVheresoeuer the body shal be, thither vvil the eagles also be gathered together.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. XVII.}}}}

''10. Vnprofitable seruants.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=How we are vnprofitable & profitable seruants.}}If our Sauiour had said that the keeping of Gods commaundements had bene vnprofitable and not auailable to our selues, then might the Protestants haue truely argued thereby that our vvorkes deserue not heauen or any revvard at Gods hand: but so he said not, but that our seruice is to God vnprofitable, who calleth for it as duety, and not as a thing needeful<noinclude>{{rh||Aa iij|or}}</noinclude>
